With so much holiday traffic, China’s transit authorities regularly deploy unfathomable resources to accommodate travelers. In all, the station reportedly handled 1,252 separate trains that day, a rate of over 52 per hour in a 24-hour period. For comparison, the incredibly busy Tokyo station of the Tokaido Shinkansen Line sees peak headways of about three minutes during major travel periods, a rate of about 480 trains per day, or 20 high-speed trains per hour. candidates.title: China's FAST telescope finds rare triple-star system still evolving
candidates.raw_excerpt:
Chinese astronomers have found a rare evolving triple-star system involving a pulsar, using the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Radio Telescope (FAST). 

The system, called J0435+3233, gives astronomers a natural lab to study how stars evolve and pull on each other, and test fundamental theories of gravity, including the strong equivalence principle. Its discovery also shows the value of combining observations across different wavelengths. The findings were published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters on Friday.

Scientists believe all three stars formed from the same cloud of gas and dust. The heaviest exploded and became the pulsar. The second evolved into a white dwarf. The lightest survived both stages and is still evolving. Eventually, it too will become a white dwarf, leaving a stable system with one pulsar and two white dwarfs.

A pulsar is a fast-spinning neutron star that fires beams of radio waves. Analyzing five years of FAST observations, scientists found this one spins once every 3.2 milliseconds and orbits a white dwarf – the dense core of a dead star – once every eight days.

Researchers combined the radio data with publicly available infrared, optical and gamma-ray data to identify a third star, with a mass similar to the Sun's. It orbits the inner pulsar-white dwarf binary once every 73.5 years on an elongated path.

The third star also explains a strange FAST reading: the pulsar's spin period is increasing by about one nanosecond a year, roughly 100 times faster than comparable pulsars. The pull of the distant companion is behind this change.

Anthropic on Thursday moved to bar users from treating its Claude artificial intelligence (AI) system with needless cruelty, amid a growing philosophical debate over whether AI can be conscious.

The San Francisco-based AI lab updated its usage policy to include "a prohibition on sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models."

"Claude's ability to end these interactions will remain the primary enforcement mechanism," the policy states.

The updated policy does not explicitly cite so-called "model welfare," the idea that AI systems might deserve types of protection usually reserved for living things, but Anthropic and its executives have openly entertained the concept.

Already last year, the company said it was giving Claude the ability to end conversations in rare, extreme cases of "persistently harmful or abusive user interactions."

Then in February, CEO Dario Amodei told The New York Times he was unsure whether AI models could be conscious.

"We don't know if the models are conscious... But we're open to the idea that it could be," Amodei said.

Science fiction and popular culture have been fascinated for decades by the boundary between technology and human intelligence, but asking whether AI is conscious may be the wrong question, according to Jackson Stakeman, a general manager at Sparq, an Atlanta-based AI services provider.

"Consciousness is a trap. We can't prove it in each other. Debate it for AI and you go in circles," Stakeman told AFP.

"The mirror is a better metaphor. These systems reflect what we put in, at scale. That's reason enough for the policy change" at Anthropic, he added.

candidates.title: AI-Powered hotline: How technology helps Beijing see, hear and act
candidates.raw_excerpt:
How can a city improve the way it listens, responds and serves its people? For a megacity like Beijing, artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming part of the answer.

Through the "Swift Response to Public Complaints" reform, Beijing's 12345 citizen hotline has handled 180 million requests from residents and enterprises over the past seven years, with a resolution rate of 97.3% and a satisfaction rate of 97.7%.

Today, AI is making the 24/7 service smarter. Inside the hotline center, large screens display real-time service data. Charts show call volumes by time period.

Operators can track daily, weekly and monthly indicators, including incoming calls, workload and connection rates.

Each operator works with a dual-screen setup. The main screen handles calls, records requests and generates service cases.  

The other provides access to a knowledge database, allowing operators to quickly search for policies and solutions while speaking.

The AI assistant helps operators recognize callers' intentions, convert speech into text, generate service records, and recommend the right departments for follow-up, allowing staff to focus more on listening and solving problems.

By reducing repetitive tasks, AI allows operators to spend more time understanding people's real needs.

The technology gives the city sharper eyes, faster responses and a deeper understanding, addressing everyday public needs with smarter solutions.

SpaceX also stated that most existing mobile devices already support this spectrum band. With this spectrum and the second-generation of Starlink Mobile satellites, SpaceX said Starlink Mobile will be “the first network operator to deploy both satellite and terrestrial spectrum,” and the network will provide “reliable service indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between.” Starlink Mobile, the direct-to-device constellation, is separate from SpaceX’s broadband internet constellation.

candidates.raw_excerpt: Parenting is hard. Why not let an AI model take over some of your childrearing duties? It may come at the expense of forming lasting emotional bonds with your progeny, but that’s a tradeoff that some AI adherents, evidently, have calculated to be worth it. OpenAI Sam Altman has bragged about how much he relies on ChatGPT to raise his son, and also thinks it’s a good idea to let an AI-generated podcast replace the “so how’d your day go?” catchup talk a mom or dad has in the car when they pick their kid up from school. Altman’s comments were ruthlessly — and rightfully — mocked at the time. But his robo-rearing ideas pale in comparison to this latest take from an AI bro. A baby can’t understand what a father is reading it, but it can recognize his voice. There’s something perverse about some of a baby’s early and formative exposure to what its father sounds like being an AI approximation. And already wanting to automate parenting duties this early on doesn’t bode well for the future. The precious time between a child and a parent doesn’t need to be streamlined, but the AI industry is obsessed with selling us on the idea of optimizing every part of our lives. Let an AI like Meta’s buzzy Muse agent send texts and emails on your behalf. Let an AI plan out your day or plan out your vacation. Let it handle bookings and reservations.

candidates.title: The Exploration Company to Test Lunar Hopper Demonstrator in 2027
candidates.raw_excerpt: Credit: The Exploration Company The Exploration Company has announced it will test a lunar hopper demonstrator called ONEIROS in the United Arab Emirates in 2027. ONEIROS is a privately funded initiative focused on validating technologies that could eventually support lower-cost access to the lunar surface. The company plans to build a one-tonne demonstrator that will use a throttleable methane-fuelled rocket engine, autonomous navigation, and hazard-avoidance systems to demonstrate the capabilities needed for controlled landings on the Moon. According to the abstract of a paper presented at the 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, work on the project began earlier this year. Teams have already built several breadboards to reduce technical risks ahead of the planned flight demonstration next year. The decision to conduct the flight demonstration in the UAE follows a memorandum of understanding signed with the country’s national space agency to support the project and develop local testing capabilities. While no subsequent binding agreement has been announced, the abstract confirmed that testing would take place in “the UAE desert.” The Exploration Company intends to follow ONEIROS with Hilal, a demonstrator designed to validate precision landing capabilities and methane/oxygen propulsion technologies on the Moon’s surface. The company will then move ahead with its full-scale Nyx Moon lander. Beyond its lunar lander programmes, The Exploration Company is also part of a consortium selected by the European Space Agency in February 2026 to conduct a Lunar Remote Camp study . Led by the Danish firm SAGA Space Architects, the consortium is developing a concept for a deployable lunar shelter that would initially support robotic operations, with the potential to accommodate astronauts during short stays on the lunar surface. candidates.title: Chinese scientists develop nuclear optical clock
candidates.raw_excerpt:
Chinese scientists have developed a nuclear optical clock that uses the nucleus of a thorium-229 atom to keep time, marking a major advance toward a new generation of highly precise clocks.

A team led by Ding Shiqian at Tsinghua University used a specially developed continuous-wave ultraviolet laser and a tiny crystal containing thorium-229 to detect and precisely measure a transition inside the atomic nucleus. The team then locked the laser's frequency to this nuclear transition, allowing the system to operate as a nuclear optical clock.

The findings were published online in Nature on Wednesday. The Chinese team and a European team achieved nuclear optical clock operation independently at around the same time.

Today's most precise optical clocks use transitions involving electrons in atoms. A nuclear optical clock instead uses a transition inside the atomic nucleus as its timing reference. Because the nucleus is much smaller than the surrounding atom, it is less susceptible to disturbances from the external environment, potentially allowing even more precise timekeeping.

The technology could also offer advantages in size and engineering, with potential applications in satellite navigation and deep-space exploration, where highly accurate timing is essential.

A major obstacle has been the need for a continuous-wave laser with a wavelength of 148 nanometers, needed to precisely drive the thorium-229 transition. Ding's team was the first to develop such a laser.

On Tuesday, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced five proposed FAA rules aiming to streamline and modernize commercial space launch and reentry regulations. The proposals take aim at the Part 450 commercial space-licensing process, trying to balance efficiency and flexibility with existing safety standards. Updating the regs is intended to help industry meet the White House’s goal of 1,000 commercial launches and reentries per year by 2030. Its to-do list includes implementing the White House’s National Space Transportation Policy and leading a commercial space transportation strategy. candidates.title: Chinese scientists develop rice's full-lifecycle cell atlas
candidates.raw_excerpt:
Chinese researchers have developed the world's first three-dimensional spatiotemporal cell atlas that tracks the entire growth lifecycle of rice.

The landmark findings, published online Tuesday in the international journal Cell, resolve long-standing bottlenecks in observing and understanding how rice cells grow, divide and coordinate to shape the crop.

Led by Yazhouwan National Laboratory based in south China's Hainan Province, a consortium of 12 research institutions, including Chinese biotech firm BGI-Research and Huazhong Agricultural University, built a 3D spatiotemporal cell atlas covering rice's entire journey, from seed germination to flowering and grain filling. The resource supports future efforts to improve grain quality, according to the team.

Using the widely cultivated japonica rice variety Zhonghua 11 as the research subject, the scientists integrated self-developed spatial omics, single-cell omics and high-throughput sequencing technologies to build a comprehensive rice cell atlas.

Covering 10 types of rice organs and tissues and 61 continuous developmental stages, the atlas is built on more than 850,000 high-quality single-nucleus datasets and over 340,000 spatial data units. The team precisely identified and annotated 119 cell types and 133 cell subtypes, successfully matching each cell's molecular features with its spatial location and dynamic changes across growth stages.

Though a government review is only just getting underway, the tech giant is already expressing remorse. In a statement to AFP , Google spokesperson Sondre Ronander admitted the company messed up, saying “we understand the concerns and have fallen short of our own high standards in this instance.” “We will study the LVV’s findings and follow their guidance,” Ronander continued. As head of the environmental department of the LVV Tommi Muilu told AFP , Google has not only felled hundreds of acres of trees, but has stripped topsoil, engineered roads and storage areas, and altered ditches.
